summary: A complaint from a Lincoln Laboratory author about the stream of questionnaires reaching ARPANET sites, especially the seven-page NCP survey of RFC 460, which gave no explanation and a two-week deadline. It asks questionnaire senders to think about the time they ask for. It is an opinion piece, not a protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: Someone grumbled that people keep sending long forms for everyone to fill out, which is a nuisance and takes time away from real work.

subtitle: A Lincoln Laboratory author complains that ARPANET sites are drowning in questionnaires, and the NCP survey was the last straw.

tldr.problem: A steady stream of questionnaires was arriving from the network community, each one a distraction from useful work.
tldr.mechanism: W. Kantrowitz argues that filling them in takes time, and that RFC 460 gave no explanation for its seven-page survey and asked for a reply in two weeks.
tldr.outcome: It is an opinion piece that asks questionnaire senders to consider the burden on small sites. It defines no protocol.

today: RFC 459 has no recorded status and is an opinion note about RFC 460. It defines no protocol.

sections.title: The Complaint
sections.content:
RFC 459, from W. Kantrowitz of LL-TX-2, says a steady stream of questionnaires has been arriving from the network community. Each one is an additional distraction from more useful work and raises the general annoyance level somewhat.

The arrival of the seven-page NCP questionnaire, RFC 460, pushed that level over the top.
sections.plainLanguage: Too many forms had arrived, and the newest one was the longest.

sections.title: Why It Bothers Sites
sections.content: The author points out that questionnaires take time to fill out, especially for someone who wants to be conscientious and answer questions that are frequently only partially applicable. He calls it presumptuous for RFC 460 to provide a lengthy questionnaire with no explanation of its motivation and then ask for a response in two weeks, while promising more questionnaires later.
sections.plainLanguage: Doing a form properly takes a while, and nobody explained why it was needed.

sections.title: The Appeal
sections.content: The note ends with a plea: sites with people who have nothing better to do than create questionnaires and other meta-work should realize that some sites run on limited personnel, have something better to do, and will get nothing done if swamped with all kinds of meta-work.
sections.plainLanguage: Small teams have real jobs to do, so please do not bury them in paperwork.
